map.Lessons 5-6, 5-7 & 5-8 — nets, surface a: Lessons 5-6, 5-7 & 5-8. Nets. Surface area of prisms. Surface area of pyramids. The end of the Brightside build.
map.Previously: the slab cured at 12 cubic m: Last time: the slab set at just 12 cubic metres. Today we paint the lot. We wrap it. We FINISH it.
map.Previously, in Episode 2: the pour went: Last time, in Episode 2: the pour went well. Fenwick's doubled bill was sent back. One week to opening day.
map.Paint for the chests, canvas for the kio: Paint for the chests. Cloth for the hut roof. Seal for the plant boxes. Each thing gets covered.
map.And \"covered\" means we need the area o: "Covered" means: we need the area of each FACE. All of them. Even the ones that hide.
map.Surface area protocol: unfold the solid: Surface area rule: unfold the solid into its net. A net is a flat map of each face. Then no face can hide from you.
map.A net is a 2-D pattern that folds into a: A net is a 2-D pattern. It folds into a 3-D solid. Surface area = the total area of the net.
map.Noah chalks candidate box patterns on th: Noah draws box patterns on the new slab. Only one folds shut.
Speed tip: count the squares FIRST. A cube has six faces. A net with five fails right away.
map.Counting is necessary, not sufficient. S: You must count. But that is not enough. Six squares can still overlap when you fold. Fold it in your head. Each face needs its own spot.
map.Reader — pick the net that actually fold: Reader, pick the net. It must fold into our cube box!
map.Which chalk pattern folds into the stora: Which pattern folds into the storage cube? Tap a net. Then tell VEX: how many faces must each cube net have?
map.Conceptual: a cube has 6 faces, so its n: Conceptual: a cube has 6 faces. So its net needs just 6 squares. AND they must fold right. Each face lands in its own spot.
map.Procedural: count squares first (elimina: Procedural: count squares first. That rules out two. For the rest, fold in your head. In a 2×3 block, squares stack on each other.
map.The supply chest: 6 long, 3 deep, 2 tall: The supply chest: 6 long, 3 deep, 2 tall. Six faces. But only three DIFFERENT ones. Each has a twin on the other side.
map.Prism protocol: top & bottom (6×3), fron: Prism rule: top & bottom (6×3), front & back (6×2), two ends (3×2). Three products. Count each one TWICE.
map.SA of a rectangular prism = 2(lw + lh +: SA of a rectangular prism = 2(lw + lh + wh). The 2 is not just for looks. Each face has a twin.
map.One can of paint covers 80 square metres: One can of paint covers 80 square metres. Tell me it is enough, reader.
map.The supply chest is a prism, 6 m × 3 m ×: The supply chest is a prism, 6 m × 3 m × 2 m. Find its total surface area. Then see: can one 80 m² can of paint cover it?
map.Conceptual: three DIFFERENT faces — top: Conceptual: three DIFFERENT faces. Top (6×3). Front (6×2). End (3×2). Each one has a twin on the other side.
Procedural: 6×3 = 18, 6×2 = 12, 3×2 = 6. Add them (36). Then DOUBLE for the twins.
map.Square pyramid roof: a 6-by-6 base and f: Square pyramid roof: a 6-by-6 base. Four triangle sides. Each has slant height 5.
map.Pyramid net: one square + four identical: Pyramid net: one square + four same triangles. Cloth covers ALL of it. The hut has a floor. Floors are faces.
map.SA of a square pyramid = base area + 4 ×: SA of a square pyramid = base area + 4 × (triangle area). Each triangle = base edge × slant ÷ 2.
map.Cut the canvas order, reader — every fac: Cut the cloth order, reader. Each face of that roof. The floor too.
map.The kiosk roof is a square pyramid: base: The hut roof is a square pyramid: base edge 6 m, slant height 5 m. Cloth covers the base AND all four triangle sides. How much cloth in all?
map.Conceptual: the pyramid's net is one squ: Conceptual: the pyramid's net: one square plus four same triangles. The base counts. The hut has a floor.
map.Procedural: base 6×6 = 36. Each triangle: Procedural: base 6×6 = 36. Each triangle: 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15. Four of them. Then add the base.
map.Opening-day eve. Fenwick's final flyer f: The night before opening day. Fenwick's last flyer flaps on the fence. One number. No doubling.
map.He added the three faces… and stopped. E: He added the three faces… and stopped. Each of those faces has a twin, Fenwick. Boss gate. Let's finish this.
map.The classic surface-area trap: finding t: The old surface-area trap. You find the three different faces. Then you forget to double them.
map.Last two jobs: weatherproof the planter: Last two jobs: seal the plant crate. Put cloth on the sandbox tent. Reader, last numbers!
And spot Fenwick's old trick. Three locks. The lot opens tomorrow.
map.Boss Gate: a prism, a pyramid, and the o: Boss Gate: a prism and a pyramid. And the oldest surface-area mistake.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. Wrap it all — an: BOSS GATE. Three locks. Wrap it all. And wrap it RIGHT.
map.Three locks before opening day: weatherp: Three locks before opening day. Seal the plant crate (4 × 4 × 2). Cover the tent (square pyramid, base edge 4, slant 3). Bust Fenwick's 36 m² chest price.
Fenwick priced the 6×3×2 chest at 36 m². His mistake:
map.Conceptual: prism = three face pairs, do: Conceptual: prism = three face pairs, doubled. Pyramid = base + 4 triangles. Look at Fenwick's number. It is HALF of a Gate 2 answer…
Procedural: Lock 1: 2(4×4 + 4×2 + 4×2). Lock 2: 4×4 + 4 × (4×3÷2). Lock 3: compare 36 to the chest's true 72.
map.Painted, wrapped, weatherproofed — and e: Painted. Wrapped. Sealed. Each square metre is counted. WE BUILT THIS.
map.THE FULL STORY: VOL. 5 — BLUEPRINT FOR B: THE FULL STORY: VOL. 5 — BLUEPRINT FOR BRIGHTSIDE. The job, the other team, and the build. Start to end.
map.Nets.A solid unfolded flat. A cube's net: Nets.A solid unfolded flat. A cube's net needs just six squares. They must fold with no overlaps.
map.SA of prisms.Three different faces, each: SA of prisms.Three different faces. Each has a twin: 2(lw + lh + wh). The chest: 2(18 + 12 + 6) = 72 m².
map.The classic trap.Adding the three faces: The classic trap.You add the three faces. You forget their twins. That is just half the truth.
map.\"To cover a thing completely, you must: "Want to cover a thing? First see each side of it." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 5 · Episode 3: Wrap It Up: did Unit 5 · Episode 3: Wrap It Up. You know nets. You can find the surface area of prisms. And of pyramids.
map.Unit 5 complete — the full Brightside sa: Unit 5 is done. The full Brightside story waits in Volume 5.
map.Test a T-shaped pattern of 6 squares: 4: Test a T-shaped pattern of 6 squares. 4 are in a column. 1 is on each side of the second square.
map.Count: 6 ✓. Fold: the column wraps into: Count: 6 ✓. Fold: the column wraps into 4 walls. The two side squares become lid and floor. No overlaps.
map.It folds clean → it's a valid net. Count: It folds clean. So it is a valid net. Count. Then fold in your head.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.How many rectangles does the net of a re: A rectangular PRISM has a net. How many rectangles are in it?
map.Double it: SA = 34 m². The ×2 is the twi: Double it: SA = 34 m². The ×2 is for the twins. Never skip it.
map.SA = 4 + 16 = 20 m². Square plus four tr: SA = 4 + 16 = 20 m². One square plus four triangles. Every time.
map.Square pyramid, base edge 4, slant 5: to: Square pyramid. Base edge 4. Slant 5. SA?
map.A rival quotes the crate at 15: exactly: Someone prices the crate at 15. That is just half of 30. They left out the twin faces.
map.The cross folds perfectly — now the coun: The cross folds just right. Now count. How many faces does a cube have?
map.The cross folds clean — six squares, six: The cross folds clean. Six squares. Six faces. No overlaps. Test passed.
map.2(18+12+6) = 72 m² — one 80 m² can cover: 2(18+12+6) = 72 m². One 80 m² can covers it. Some paint is left. Fenwick's 'best' price is already beaten.
map.That's the three faces WITHOUT their twi: That is the three faces WITHOUT their twins. The chest also has a back and a bottom. And a far end.
map.You added the edges. Surface area multip: You added the edges. Surface area: multiply each face first. Do length × width per face.
map.Three face pairs: 6×3, 6×2, 3×2 — sum th: Three face pairs: 6×3, 6×2, 3×2. Add them. Then double.
map.36 + 4(15) = 96 m² of canvas. The roof —: 36 + 4(15) = 96 m² of cloth. The roof and the floor are covered.
map.Those are just the four triangles — the: Those are just the four triangles. The hut has a floor. Floors are faces.
map.You counted four BASES. There's one squa: You counted four BASES. There is one square base. The triangles come in fours.
map.One square (6×6) plus four triangles (6: One square (6×6) plus four triangles (6 × 5 ÷ 2 each). Add them all.
map.Lock 3 holds. 36 is exactly HALF of the: Lock 3 holds. 36 is just HALF of the chest's true 72. Which mistake cuts a surface area in half?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 64 m² sealed, 40 m² stit: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 64 m² sealed. 40 m² sewn. Fenwick's half-true price is gone for good. BRIGHTSIDE OPENS TOMORROW.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
